index.title: Troubleshooting
index.subtitle: Guided troubleshooting checklists for your 2-stroke outboard engines. Always start with the global checklist: compression, spark, fuel — in that order.
index.empty: No 2-stroke outboard engine in your fleet.
index.eligibilityHint: Troubleshooting checklists apply to 2-stroke outboard engines. Set the kind to "outboard" and the cycle to "2-stroke" on an engine's page to see it listed here.

firstContactCard.title: Buying used: first contact
firstContactCard.text: Going to see a used engine? Follow the first-contact sheet to assess it on the spot without missing anything.

common.resetConfirm: Reset this checklist? All checked steps for this engine will be unchecked.
common.resetSheetConfirm: Reset this sheet? Its checked steps will be unchecked for this engine.
common.neverDry: This sheet involves starting the engine: always in a water tub or with flushing muffs, never dry. A few seconds dry is enough to destroy the impeller.
common.localStateHint: This sheet is not tied to any engine in your fleet: checkboxes are not saved and start fresh on your next visit.

global.title: Global checklist — the golden rule
global.intro: Compression → Spark → Fuel. Always in that order. Fuel is tested last even though it is the cause in 7 to 8.5 cases out of 10, only because it is the cheapest repair. Without compression, nothing else matters. Steps are ordered from cheapest to most expensive.

flywheel.label: Flywheel turned by hand through 360° — no hard spot

gearshift.label: Gears: propeller free in neutral, resistant in forward and reverse

kill_switch.label: Kill switch in place and in the run position

fresh_fuel.label: Fresh fuel, properly mixed (50:1 unless spec says otherwise), no water

fuel_system.label: Fuel system followed end to end

timing.label: Everything checks out and it still won't run: timing

warnings.waterOnly: Always in a water tub or with flushing muffs. Never dry.

compression.title: Low or uneven compression
compression.intro: Test: spark plugs removed, gauge threaded into the plug hole, 5 to 8 pulls of the starter rope (or 2 to 4 s on the electric starter), on every cylinder, gauge zeroed between readings.

spread_calculated.label: Spread between cylinders calculated
spread_calculated.detail: That is criterion #1, not the raw value.

model_spec.label: Model spec checked
model_spec.detail: Some Johnson/Evinrude 9.5s run perfectly fine at 60–68 PSI.

retest_after_run.label: Engine sat unused for a long time? Retest after a few hours of running

retest_after_head.label: After any cylinder head removal: recheck once torqued to spec

warnings.gauges: Gauges vary wildly: a €20 model reads 10 to 15 PSI lower than a professional one. Compare cylinders against each other, never numbers from two different gauges.

notes.over_spread: If the spread exceeds 12%: rings, scored cylinder, or head gasket. That is the expensive repair — when buying, negotiate very low or walk away.

kill_circuit.label: Kill circuit: disconnect the black/yellow wire at the power pack and retest
kill_circuit.detail: Spark back = fault in the stop circuit (key switch, harness, corroded terminals).

plugs.label: New spark plugs, gap checked with a tool (they are not set at the factory), same brand everywhere

coils.label: Coils: visual inspection of the gel on the back
coils.detail: Dry, cracked, or melted = dead coil. It is the ignition component that fails most often.

rectifier.label: Rectifier: disconnect the yellow wires and retest (2 seconds, rare case but free)

cranking_rpm.label: Cranking speed ≥ 250 rpm (otherwise battery, cables, or starter)

grounds.label: Grounds clean, corrosion-free, tight — especially the coil grounds

model_id.label: Model + year identified on crowleymarine.com (e.g. J50PLEA = Johnson 50 hp 1999)

cdi_measures.label: Stator / timer base / power pack measured in ohms per the CDI guide
cdi_measures.detail: Sample readings: stator brown ↔ brown/yellow 650–850 Ω (CDI) or 750–950 Ω (OEM); timer base white ↔ green and white ↔ blue 25–30 Ω. A value inside either range is enough.

warnings.weak_spark: A spark visible on the tester can still be too weak under compression. If everything else checks out and one cylinder is not firing, try a coil.

notes.triage_all: Triage rule: no spark on any cylinder → look for what is shared (kill switch, stator, power pack).
notes.triage_one: No spark on a single cylinder → that cylinder's plug or coil.
notes.dva: Peak voltages require a DVA adapter. If the resistance is good, the voltage almost always is too.

fuel.title: Fuel supply (culprit #1)
fuel.intro: Physically follow the path: tank → hose + primer bulb → filter → pump → carburetor → reed valves.

fresh_fuel.label: Fuel less than a month old, properly mixed, no water

black_hose_only.label: Black automotive fuel hose only
black_hose_only.detail: Grey hoses have a liner that ethanol dissolves (debris in the carburetor).

primer_bulb.label: Primer bulb fitted following the arrows, it must get completely firm

air_leaks.label: Hunt for air leaks: every clamp, every quick connector

filter_direction.label: Filter clean and fitted the right way (arrow)

pump_test.label: Pump test: engine dies after 20–60 s? Restart while squeezing the primer bulb continuously
pump_test.detail: If it stays alive on the bulb → pump is dead.

pump_replace.label: Replace with a new assembled pump rather than a kit

carb_photos.label: Photos of hoses and linkages before disassembly

carb_removal.label: Removal: air box, hoses, linkage, 2 nuts

carb_disassembly.label: Disassembly: bowl, float, needle valve, every jet

mixture_screw_count.label: Mixture screw: count the turns while backing it out

carb_cleaner.label: Carb cleaner in every hole and orifice, generously — nothing can be damaged

cork_float.label: Cork float → replace with a plastic one outright

float_level.label: Float level even on every axis (adjust the tab)

blow_test.label: Blow test
blow_test.detail: Bowl down → air passes; carburetor upside down → no air passes.

reassembly.label: Reassembly, then mixture screw adjustment
reassembly.detail: Screw gently seated, backed out 1 to 1¼ turn, fine-tuned by ¼ turn with 20–30 s to react.

reed_backfire.label: Fuel spitting back out of the carburetor throat, or backfiring?

reed_backlight.label: Reeds against the light: light visible between the petals = replace

choke_only.symptom: Only runs with the choke on

leaking.symptom: Fuel dripping while squeezing the primer bulb
leaking.cause: Stuck float / needle valve no longer sealing

flooding.cause: Worn needle valve, punctured float, enrichment solenoid powered permanently (~5.5 ± 1.5 Ω)

dry_plugs.symptom: Dry plugs, no fuel at all

telltale_nipple.label: Tell-tale nipple: insect nests, mud — run a thin wire through the nipple and its hose

thermostat.label: Thermostat: remove it and run again
thermostat.detail: 5 minutes, it settles the question immediately. Corroded shut = classic.

impeller.label: Impeller: curled, dry, or cracked vanes = replace (~€15, THE #1 maintenance item)
impeller.detail: Gearcase in reverse before removal, do not lose the key, liquid soap on reassembly.

drill_test.label: Test before refitting the gearcase: drill on the driveshaft → water must squirt out of the outlet port

water_tube.label: New impeller but still nothing? Misaligned copper water tube or clogged internal passages
water_tube.detail: The grommet must seat properly. Garden hose test into the water tube: water must come out at the thermostat housing.

water_jackets.label: Blocked water jackets (sand, scale): remove the head cover, sometimes the powerhead
water_jackets.detail: Heaviest level, everything else must be ruled out first.

ir_thermometer.label: Check: infrared thermometer on the head near the spark plug

warnings.no_thermostat: Do not run without a thermostat: an engine running too cold wears just like one running too hot.

notes.used_engine: Worth remembering: on a used engine "that overheats", the previous owner has often already replaced the impeller and removed the thermostat with no result. Do not trust past repairs: run the checklist again from the top.

gear_oil.label: Milky or grey gearcase oil = water → seals to redo

shear_pin.label: Slipping propeller, small engines: broken shear pin
shear_pin.detail: It must stick out in a T on both sides of the hub — a €3 part.

spun_hub.label: Slipping propeller, bigger engines: spun hub
spun_hub.detail: Feels like cavitation under acceleration → re-hub or replace.

shift_linkage.label: Stiff or dead gear shifting: check the linkage and cables first, before opening the gearcase

corroded_gearcase.label: Gearcase welded on by corrosion: gentle escalation
corroded_gearcase.detail: Bolts first (penetrating oil + heat), then progressively bigger putty knives in the parting line, then a progressive pry bar.

grease_splines.label: On reassembly: grease splines and threads

warnings.cold_shift: In severe cold, the shift rod becomes brittle.

battery.label: Battery charged, terminals clean and tight — always start there

solenoid_jump.label: Click without rotation: jump the solenoid's two large posts
solenoid_jump.detail: Starter spins → dead solenoid. It does not spin → dead starter.

solenoid_welded.label: Welded solenoid: with a multimeter, any continuity between the posts with the key out = stuck contacts → replace

runaway_starter.label: Starter that keeps spinning with the engine running: disconnect the battery immediately
runaway_starter.detail: Short circuit in the relay or the button.

connections.label: Connections redone properly: crimped terminals then heat-shrink tubing

trim_wiring.label: Trim dead at one station only: follow the blue/green wires
trim_wiring.detail: A cut wire is more likely than a dead trim motor. At-sea workaround: manual tilt release screw.

timing.title: Timing and link & sync
timing.intro: When: after a carburetor rebuild, after replacing the timer base / stator / power pack, after touching any linkage, or on an unknown used engine showing the symptoms below. Not systematically.

shop_manual.label: Shop manual for the model in hand
shop_manual.detail: No generic value replaces the engine's spec.

cam_roller.label: Cam follower roller present and intact (often broken on old engines)

fast_start_modules.label: "Fast start" / S.L.O.W. modules disconnected if the manual says so

tdc_pointer.label: Timing pointer verified against true TDC of cylinder #1
tdc_pointer.detail: Two positions with identical rod depth: TDC is in the middle.

wot_stop.label: Wide-open-throttle stop: butterflies horizontal
wot_stop.detail: The stop screw ends the travel, never the carburetor's internal stops.

max_advance.label: Max advance set to spec, never beyond
max_advance.detail: Orders of magnitude: ~34° BTDC old Mercury crossflow, ~21° direct charge, 19–28° OMC crossflow.

pickup_timing.label: Throttle pickup: cam mark aligned with the center of the roller
pickup_timing.detail: The throttle starts opening around 3–5° BTDC.

warm_mixture.label: Engine warm in the water: mixture fine-tuned by ¼ turn

idle_rpm.label: Idle 700–800 rpm in neutral, 550–650 rpm in gear

cable_preload.label: Cable reconnected with a slight preload against the idle stop

no_start.symptom: Won't start despite compression + spark + clean carburetor

high_idle.symptom: Idle too high, screw at its stop

acceleration_gap.lead: Pickup too early or too late

warnings.max_advance: Excessive max advance burns holes in pistons. When in doubt, set it retarded.

notes.single_carb: Single carburetor (4–15 hp): the "sync" part disappears. If the engine has no adjustable advance stop, it comes down to cam/roller alignment + mixture screw + idle stop, no timing light.

first_contact.title: First contact (buying used)
first_contact.intro: To run on the spot, in front of the seller, before any negotiation.

gearshift.label: Gears: neutral free, forward and reverse resistant

compression.label: Compression on every cylinder
compression.detail: A seller who refuses this test is often hiding something.

gear_oil.label: Gearcase oil drained a little: milky = water

external_tank.label: Clean external tank with fresh fuel — never the boat's own

primer_bulb.label: Primer bulb that firms up, no leak, no air noise

start_listen.label: Start it and listen to how it behaves

notes.deal_breakers: Deal breakers: seized piston, gearcase that will not shift.

ai.title: AI assistant — troubleshooting
ai.disclaimer: The AI recommends, it does not decide: its advice does not replace your engine model's service manual.
ai.empty: Describe the failure symptoms, or run an analysis of your checklist progress.
ai.placeholder: E.g.: the engine starts then stalls after 30 seconds, the primer bulb stays soft…
ai.causesTitle: Probable causes, from cheapest to most expensive
